questions.prompt: Four ranks participate in one synchronous training step. A separate inference service has four independent replicas. One training rank slows down. What is the most defensible immediate consequence?

choices.text: The training group may wait for its required participant; the inference service is not automatically part of that barrier.
Every service using the same data center must wait for the training rank.
choices.feedback_incorrect: A shared location does not establish a shared synchronization group. Other services might share resource contention, but they do not automatically participate in this barrier.

choices.text: The training result is necessarily corrupted as soon as one rank is delayed.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Delay can increase waiting without making the calculation incorrect. Correctness depends on the operation and state protocol.

choices.text: The scheduler can always replace that rank with any idle inference replica during the step.
choices.feedback_incorrect: A replacement must have the supported membership, state and role. An arbitrary device cannot be inserted into an in-flight collective.

questions.feedback_correct: The dependency belongs to the declared training group. A performance stall is not, by itself, evidence of corrupted state or a shared barrier with independent services.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The dependency belongs to the declared training group. A performance stall is not, by itself, evidence of corrupted state or a shared barrier with independent services.

questions.prompt: Before approving more accelerators for the workload, which evidence would help evaluate useful scaling? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The workload’s communication and synchronization groups.
Measured throughput or service latency, together with the relevant step-time distribution.
Available fabric, data-supply, power and cooling capacity.
The accelerator count alone, without workload or resource measurements.

questions.feedback_correct: Workload dependencies, useful-progress measurements and supporting capacity together explain the proposed expansion. Device count is an inventory measure, not a scaling result.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Select the dependency, measurement and capacity evidence. Count alone cannot show whether extra devices will produce useful progress.

questions.prompt: Four data-parallel ranks contribute scalar gradients 2, 4, 6 and 8. The declared operation sums them and then divides by four. What value should every participating rank use for this averaged gradient?

choices.text: 8, because the last arriving contribution replaces the earlier ones.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Arrival order is not a last-write-wins rule for this collective. All four contributions belong to the declared reduction.

choices.text: 5, because the sum of the four declared contributions is divided by four.
20, because sum reduction always performs averaging automatically.
choices.feedback_incorrect: 20 is the sum before the separate division. A sum reduction does not by itself imply averaging.

choices.text: A different value on each rank, because each rank must own a different model shard.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Data-parallel replicas are not necessarily different model shards. The operation specifies the same aggregate for each participant.

questions.feedback_correct: The sum is 20; the explicitly declared division gives 5. In this teaching example every data-parallel rank receives the same aggregate. Reduction and averaging are distinct operations.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sum is 20; the explicitly declared division gives 5. In this teaching example every data-parallel rank receives the same aggregate. Reduction and averaging are distinct operations.

questions.prompt: A supported framework is changing a training job’s worker-group membership at a recovery boundary. Which items should the recovery plan define? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Which committed model, optimizer and input-progress state must be restored.
How membership, roles and communication groups are re-established.
Timeouts, retry budgets and checks before resuming useful work.
A rule allowing any replacement GPU to consume in-flight messages under the failed rank’s identity immediately.

questions.feedback_correct: Recovery needs coherent state, supported group setup and bounded behavior. Reusing a failed participant’s identity without those checks is not a recovery protocol.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Select state restoration, group re-establishment and bounded validation. An in-flight identity shortcut can confuse membership and operation state.

questions.prompt: A correlated trace shows receipt of message 17 at 10:00:00.003 on B and its send at 10:00:00.005 on A. What should the engineer conclude first?

choices.text: The message must have traveled backward in time.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Unsynchronized or uncertain timestamps can invert the displayed order. They do not invert the message’s causal dependency.

choices.text: The model must have accepted the wrong gradient.
choices.feedback_incorrect: The trace alone does not show an incorrect model update. Inspect operation identity and runtime behavior before diagnosing correctness.

choices.text: Check clock offset and uncertainty, then use the matching message identity and dependency to interpret the sequence.
Discard all physical timestamps because they can never be useful.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Physical timestamps remain useful when interpreted with their uncertainty and corroborating identifiers.

questions.feedback_correct: The matching message establishes a send/receive dependency. Cross-clock timestamps require an uncertainty or alignment check; the apparent inversion alone proves neither backward causality nor model corruption.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The matching message establishes a send/receive dependency. Cross-clock timestamps require an uncertainty or alignment check; the apparent inversion alone proves neither backward causality nor model corruption.

questions.prompt: A synchronous job has stable average latency but inconsistent step completion. Which evidence helps distinguish causes? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Per-step tails and the readiness times of required participants.
Queue, retransmission and accelerator-compute evidence correlated with the affected steps.
Message or operation identifiers and the uncertainty of cross-host timestamps.
Peak link speed alone as proof that the fabric cannot be involved.

questions.feedback_correct: Tails expose waiting, layer-specific signals test alternative causes, and identifiers plus timestamp uncertainty support correlation. Peak speed does not rule out congestion, loss or slow participants.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Select readiness/tail evidence, correlated system signals and trace identity/time uncertainty. Peak link rate alone cannot diagnose the stall.

questions.prompt: A regional GPU consumer uses four equal-sized batches per second. Its buffer initially holds eight batches. Supply drops to two batches per second for three seconds. Under this simplified flow model, what happens?

choices.text: The consumer starves immediately when supply drops.
choices.feedback_incorrect: The buffer covers the short deficit in this scenario. Its initial eight batches exceed the six-batch shortfall.

choices.text: The buffer falls to two batches and supplies the consumer throughout the three-second dip.
The buffer grows to fourteen batches.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Consumption exceeds supply, so the buffer drains rather than grows: 8 minus (4 minus 2) times 3 equals 2.

choices.text: Private connectivity makes the buffer calculation unnecessary.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Connection type does not remove the stated supply and consumption rates or guarantee an uninterrupted service.

questions.feedback_correct: The deficit is two batches per second for three seconds, so six buffered batches are consumed and two remain. Longer deficits can exhaust the buffer, but starvation is not immediate.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The deficit is two batches per second for three seconds, so six buffered batches are consumed and two remain. Longer deficits can exhaust the buffer, but starvation is not immediate.

questions.prompt: Which requirements belong in a cross-provider inference deployment review? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Model-version rollout, routing and session-compatibility policy.
Data-location policy, identity/key ownership and recovery authority.
Capacity, path/failover behavior and measured latency or loss objectives.
A universal requirement that every region changes model version at the exact same instant, regardless of service policy.

questions.feedback_correct: The review needs explicit service, governance and link contracts. Coordinated global model cutover is one possible policy, not a rule for every inference deployment.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Select the service policy, administrative controls and operating-link evidence. Simultaneous worldwide updates are not universally necessary.

questions.prompt: Training group A loses a worker. Independent group B is healthy. A replacement resource is available, but its required power/cooling envelope has not been checked. What is the best next action?

choices.text: Resume A immediately because available accelerator count is the only admission criterion.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Inventory alone does not show safe power, cooling, communication or state readiness.

choices.text: Roll back every job at the facility because any AI failure requires global recovery.
choices.feedback_incorrect: A failure in one group does not establish a dependency requiring facility-wide rollback.

choices.text: Bound recovery to A using the supported framework, verify required state and resource readiness, and resume only after the checks pass.
Disable checkpointing so the replacement cannot load an older state.
choices.feedback_incorrect: A committed checkpoint can provide a defined recovery state. Removing it does not make a replacement coherent.

questions.feedback_correct: The affected group and its resource envelope define the recovery decision. Preserve a healthy independent group unless actual shared-resource evidence requires broader action.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The affected group and its resource envelope define the recovery decision. Preserve a healthy independent group unless actual shared-resource evidence requires broader action.

questions.prompt: Which items make an automated recovery decision reviewable? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A declared affected group, failure boundary and authorized actor.
A tested state-restoration procedure, bounded retries and an escalation path.
Correlated telemetry and explicit readiness/exit checks before resuming.
A dashboard’s green device count alone, without workload or state evidence.

questions.feedback_correct: Authority and scope, a tested recovery procedure, bounded action and evidence-based readiness checks make the decision explainable. Device count alone cannot establish service or training readiness.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Select scope/authority, tested bounded recovery and correlated readiness evidence. A green count does not replace those checks.
